Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Participants in the lowest 25(OH)D quartile were more likely to report depressive symptoms than those in the highest quartile.
Sentence: "When investigating the relationship between the presence versus absence of depressive symptoms and quartiles of 25(OH)D, participants in the lowest quartile were more likely to report depressive symptoms compared with those in the highest quartile."
Measured as: presence of depressive symptoms (CES-D)
Population: 615 non-clinical young adults in Dunedin, New Zealand
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D quartile (measured, not given)
Comparator: Highest 25(OH)D quartile
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 615
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Lifetime diagnosis of major depressive disorder was not significantly associated with vitamin D concentrations.
Sentence: "Symptoms of depression and the lifetime diagnosis of MDD were not significantly associated with vitamin D concentrations."
Measured as: lifetime diagnosis of MDD (CID-S)
Population: General population sample from the Study of Health in Pomerania (SHIP-1)
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D level (measured, not given)
Comparator: Lower versus higher vitamin D levels
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 1,908
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
